comments.text:
THE MORE YOU KNOW!
Watching this video made me realise I almost fell for this scam.
A decade ago or so me and my mom went to Cancun and the resort offered a tour around and that at the end they would give us freebies (T-Shirts, a bag and a tequila). We went thinking it was a legit tour of the resort.
The woman was brazillian like us, so there was no language barrier, she made us tons of questions about us, where we lived, if we liked to travel, how often we traveled, WHERE we liked to go etc. It was odd for me, but I was just a 19yo.
She then took us to make a tour... but not the facilities in the resort (as I believed) but of their "exclusive" accomodations, and like VIP areas and talked about the many perks on becoming a member of the resort "club", so to say (is a chain of resorts all around the world).
Then after showing us all of that she took us to a place with tons of other sellers doing their stuff, we got sat on a table with this guy (also brazillian) and tried to sold us really hard.
I was almost saying to my mom to do it, since she was very conflicted and turning to a straight "no", but this guy got impatient i guess and tried an aggressive approach.
For context: during that time in my hometwon the police was going on a strike and was a chaos with criminals going for each others and stealing stores (fr, it was almost a "purge" scenario). This guy, that obviously received the forms with our information to study before the woman brought us to the final strike, went like "do you really wanna go back to your home? with all that chaos happenning?", in a tone almost mocking my home. Listen, I may say the bad things about my country, but dont you ever DARE to insult the land I was birthed into. I instantly switched to hating that whole stupidity all together.
The sellers seemed frustrated and irritaded but we got to go with our freebies and no contract signed. All crap of course.
And I never forgot the feeling of how all of that was so weird... and the precious hours of our expensive trip they fucking wasted. And I only wanted to know where the fucking spa was.
BUT REGARDLESS, I must say that this video made me finally realise that there was a name for what happenned, and it was 100% a devil's scam LOL Thank God my mom was always so grounded with money.

comments.author: @Zimbu-e4y
comments.text: My wife and I went to a presentation back in the mid 80s to get a promised 3 day cruise. We sat thru an agonizing 5 hour high pressure pitch and property tour. The crazy math they use to make it sound cheap is phenomenal. The price surprised me. At that time it was about $20k for 1 week every August, which almost made it seem like it could work - almost. After saying no about 1000 times we get taken back to the managers office. Now the gloves came off and the pressure went off the charts (these slime balls are good at their job). We again said no about 20 more times. The mgr finally turned to the sales lady and said, "Well, I guess these people just aren't time share material." He flung the free cruise papers across the desk at me, I had to catch them as they slid off. Then the 2 of them got up and started walking out of the office and down the hall. We followed them thinking they were walking us out. The mgr stops, turns around and says, "No, were going to lunch. Had you bought you could have joined us. You can go back around the corner and there's a door out back you can use." When we exited, I turned to my wife, "Boy, don't let the door hit you in the ass on the way out!" We both laughed, got in our car and drove to get a nice lunch of our own and then home. We did get the 3 day cruise though. And, it was one of our favorite vacations. But, the hoops we needed to jump thru to actually get it are a whole other story. So, all in all, I don't feel the presentation was s complete waste of our time, but only because we were able to say NO!
